lesson_1.topicLabel: Enquiry 01: Ice Age Hunters & Sunken Doggerland
lesson_1.title: How Did Stone Age Hunters Survive and How Did Britain Become an Island?
lesson_1.spokenTitle: How did Stone Age hunters survive, and how did Britain become an island?
lesson_1.provenanceNote: British Museum, Royal BC Museum, Historic Environment Scotland & Original Hub Cartography (Zero AI Imagery)

cards.heading: Ice Age Caves & Flint Handaxes
cards.stat: Happisburgh Footprints & Chipped Flint Tools
cards.connective: How did Stone Age hunters survive, and how did Britain become an island?
cards.html: During the freezing Old Stone Age, families sheltered inside limestone caves like Creswell Crags. Makers chipped sharp flint handaxes and tracked giant woolly mammoths for food and warm hides.
cards.spoken: How did Stone Age hunters survive, and how did Britain become an island? <short pause> During the freezing Old Stone Age , families sheltered inside limestone caves like Creswell Crags . Makers chipped sharp flint handaxes and tracked giant woolly mammoths for food and warm hides.

cards.heading: Cheddar Man & Antler Masks
cards.stat: Gough's Cave Skeleton & Star Carr Lake Camp
cards.connective: Around ten thousand BC, the Ice Age ended and green forests spread.
cards.html: Hunter-gatherers fished rivers and moved camp with the seasons as red deer filled new woods. Archaeologists found Cheddar Man in Somerset and carved antler headdresses at Star Carr.
cards.spoken: Around ten thousand BC, the Ice Age ended and green forests spread. <short pause> Hunter-gatherers fished rivers and moved camp with the seasons as red deer filled new woods. Archaeologists found Cheddar Man in Somerset and carved antler headdresses at Star Carr.

cards.heading: Sinking of Green Doggerland
cards.stat: Melting Ice Floods the North Sea Land Bridge
cards.connective: For thousands of years, families could still walk dry-footed from Europe.
cards.html: Hunters camped across Doggerland, a wide green land bridge linking Britain to Europe. Around 6500 BC, melting ice sheets flooded those low marshes under the North Sea.
cards.spoken: For thousands of years, families could still walk dry-footed from Europe. <short pause> Hunters camped across Doggerland , a wide green land bridge linking Britain to Europe. Around 6500 BC , melting ice sheets flooded those low marshes under the North Sea .

cards.heading: Britain Becomes an Island
cards.stat: Mammoth Teeth Dredged from the Sea Floor
cards.connective: Rising waves changed Britain's map and Stone Age life forever.
cards.html: Flooding Doggerland cut Britain off from mainland Europe as an island. Clever Stone Age families had survived freezing ice, warming forests, and rising seas.
cards.spoken: Rising waves changed Britain's map and Stone Age life forever. <short pause> Flooding Doggerland cut Britain off from mainland Europe as an island . Clever Stone Age families had survived freezing ice, warming forests, and rising seas.

lesson_1.takeaway: Stone Age hunter-gatherers survived the Ice Age with chipped flint tools before melting ice flooded Doggerland around 6500 BC and turned Britain into an island.
vocab: 1. Palaeolithic
The Old Stone Age when Ice Age hunters chipped flint handaxes.
2. Knapping
Striking flint stones carefully to chip off razor-sharp tool flakes.
3. Doggerland
Green land bridge to Europe flooded by the North Sea around 6500 BC.
lesson_1.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Stone Age hunter-gatherers survived the Ice Age with chipped flint tools before melting ice flooded Doggerland around 6500 BC and turned Britain into an island.

lesson_2.topicLabel: Enquiry 02: The First Farmers & Skara Brae
lesson_2.title: How Did Farming and Stone Villages Change Stone Age Life?
lesson_2.spokenTitle: How did farming and stone villages change Stone Age life?
lesson_2.provenanceNote: British Museum, Royal BC Museum, Historic Environment Scotland & Original Hub Cartography (Zero AI Imagery)

cards.heading: Boats Bring the First Farms
cards.stat: Wheat, Sheep & Polished Stone Axes Arrive
cards.connective: How did farming and stone villages change Stone Age life?
cards.html: Around 4000 BC, newcomers sailed wooden boats to Britain with tame sheep, cattle, and wheat seeds. Using polished stone axes and flint sickles, Neolithic farmers cleared woods for crops.
cards.spoken: How did farming and stone villages change Stone Age life? <short pause> Around 4000 BC, newcomers sailed wooden boats to Britain with tame sheep, cattle, and wheat seeds . Using polished stone axes and flint sickles, Neolithic farmers cleared woods for crops.

cards.heading: Storm Uncovers Skara Brae
cards.stat: 8 Snug Orkney Flagstone Homes Found in 1850
cards.connective: Steady harvests meant families could build lasting villages all year round.
cards.html: In 1850, a winter storm in Orkney uncovered Skara Brae beneath tall sand dunes. Eight flagstone houses still held stone box beds, warm central hearths, and stone dressers.
cards.spoken: Steady harvests meant families could build lasting villages all year round. <short pause> In 1850, a winter storm in Orkney uncovered Skara Brae beneath tall sand dunes. Eight flagstone houses still held stone box beds , warm central hearths, and stone dressers .

cards.heading: West Kennet Long Barrow
cards.stat: Nearly 50 Ancestors Placed in Stone Chambers
cards.connective: Settled farming villages also honoured their ancestors on high hills.
cards.html: Villagers in Wiltshire raised West Kennet Long Barrow with heavy boulders guarding five dark chambers. Families placed nearly fifty ancestors inside beside hand-coiled clay bowls and beads.
cards.spoken: Settled farming villages also honoured their ancestors on high hills. <short pause> Villagers in Wiltshire raised West Kennet Long Barrow with heavy boulders guarding five dark chambers. Families placed nearly fifty ancestors inside beside hand-coiled clay bowls and beads.

cards.heading: From Roaming Camps to Villages
cards.stat: Year-Round Villages, Pottery & Ancestor Tombs
cards.connective: Farming transformed how families lived, ate, and worked together.
cards.html: Instead of moving camp every season, Neolithic families lived in permanent villages all year. Growing crops, making clay pottery, and building barrows rooted communities to their land.
cards.spoken: Farming transformed how families lived, ate, and worked together. <short pause> Instead of moving camp every season, Neolithic families lived in permanent villages all year. Growing crops, making clay pottery , and building barrows rooted communities to their land.

lesson_2.takeaway: Around 4000 BC, Neolithic farming let families settle in year-round villages like stone-built Skara Brae and raise giant ancestor tombs like West Kennet Long Barrow.
vocab: 1. Neolithic
The New Stone Age when Britain's first farmers built settled villages.
2. Skara Brae
5,000-year-old Orkney stone village uncovered by a storm in 1850.
3. Long Barrow
Long chalk-and-earth mound with stone chambers for village ancestors.
lesson_2.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Around 4000 BC, Neolithic farming let families settle in year-round villages like stone-built Skara Brae and raise giant ancestor tombs like West Kennet Long Barrow.

lesson_3.title: How and Why Did Stone Age People Build Giant Stonehenge?
lesson_3.spokenTitle: How and why did Stone Age people build giant Stonehenge?
lesson_3.provenanceNote: British Museum, Royal BC Museum, Historic Environment Scotland & Original Hub Cartography (Zero AI Imagery)

cards.heading: Chalk Henge & Welsh Bluestones
cards.stat: 80 Bluestones Hauled 140 Miles from Wales
cards.connective: How and why did Stone Age people build giant Stonehenge?
cards.html: Around 3000 BC, workers dug a circular chalk henge on Salisbury Plain using antler picks. Later, teams hauled eighty spotted bluestones 140 miles from the Preseli Hills in Wales.
cards.spoken: How and why did Stone Age people build giant Stonehenge? <short pause> Around 3000 BC, workers dug a circular chalk henge on Salisbury Plain using antler picks . Later, teams hauled eighty spotted bluestones 140 miles from the Preseli Hills in Wales.

cards.heading: Sarsen Arches & Feast Village
cards.stat: 25-Tonne Sarsens Locked into Tall Trilithons
cards.connective: Next, builders dragged even bigger grey sandstone boulders across Wiltshire.
cards.html: Without wheels or cranes, crews pulled 25-tonne sarsens on wooden sledges and locked them into three-stone trilithons. Nearby at Durrington Walls, builders shared huge winter pork feasts.
cards.spoken: Next, builders dragged even bigger grey sandstone boulders across Wiltshire. <short pause> Without wheels or cranes, crews pulled 25-tonne sarsens on wooden sledges and locked them into three-stone trilithons . Nearby at Durrington Walls , builders shared huge winter pork feasts.

cards.heading: The Heel Stone & Solstice Sun
cards.stat: Aligned with Midsummer & Midwinter Sunbeams
cards.connective: Careful stone positions lined the circle up with the sky.
cards.html: Outside the circle stands the lone Heel Stone watching the horizon. At the Midsummer solstice sunrise and Midwinter sunset, sunlight shines straight through Stonehenge's giant stone arches.
cards.spoken: Careful stone positions lined the circle up with the sky. <short pause> Outside the circle stands the lone Heel Stone watching the horizon. At the Midsummer solstice sunrise and Midwinter sunset, sunlight shines straight through Stonehenge's giant stone arches.

cards.heading: Giant Stone Calendar & Shrine
cards.stat: Built Over Centuries Without Metal or Wheels
cards.connective: Hundreds of years of teamwork left an unforgettable monument.
cards.html: Working without metal tools, Neolithic communities united thousands of helpers across Britain. Together they raised Stonehenge as a sacred solar calendar and gathering place for ancestors.
cards.spoken: Hundreds of years of teamwork left an unforgettable monument. <short pause> Working without metal tools, Neolithic communities united thousands of helpers across Britain. Together they raised Stonehenge as a sacred solar calendar and gathering place for ancestors.

lesson_3.takeaway: Using antler picks, wooden sledges, and huge teamwork, Stone Age builders hauled Welsh bluestones and 25-tonne sarsens to align Stonehenge with the solstice sun.
vocab: 1. Henge
Circular prehistoric earthwork with an inner ditch and outer bank.
2. Trilithon
Giant three-stone arch with two uprights and one top lintel.
3. Solstice
Longest summer day or shortest winter day aligned with Stonehenge.
lesson_3.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Using antler picks, wooden sledges, and huge teamwork, Stone Age builders hauled Welsh bluestones and 25-tonne sarsens to align Stonehenge with the solstice sun.

lesson_4.topicLabel: Enquiry 04: Enter the Bronze Age & Beaker People
lesson_4.title: How Did Beaker Newcomers and Bronze Metal Change Life in Britain?
lesson_4.spokenTitle: How did Beaker newcomers and bronze metal change life in Britain?
lesson_4.provenanceNote: British Museum, Royal BC Museum, Historic Environment Scotland & Original Hub Cartography (Zero AI Imagery)

cards.heading: Beaker Folk & Copper Mines
cards.stat: Great Orme Copper & Cornish Tin Smelted
cards.connective: How did Beaker newcomers and bronze metal change life in Britain?
cards.html: Around 2400 BC, the Beaker people arrived from Europe with patterned clay pots and metalworking skills. Miners dug green copper at Great Orme and smelted rock over fierce fires.
cards.spoken: How did Beaker newcomers and bronze metal change life in Britain? <short pause> Around 2400 BC, the Beaker people arrived from Europe with patterned clay pots and metalworking skills. Miners dug green copper at Great Orme and smelted rock over fierce fires.

cards.heading: Casting Tough Golden Bronze
cards.stat: 9 Parts Copper + 1 Part Tin in Stone Moulds
cards.connective: Pure copper bent too easily, so smiths blended two metals together.
cards.html: Clever smiths mixed nine parts copper with one part Cornish tin to make tough bronze. Poured into hollow two-piece moulds, bronze axes cleared woodland fast and could be recast.
cards.spoken: Pure copper bent too easily, so smiths blended two metals together. <short pause> Clever smiths mixed nine parts copper with one part Cornish tin to make tough bronze . Poured into hollow two-piece moulds, bronze axes cleared woodland fast and could be recast.

cards.heading: Gold Capes & Amesbury Archer
cards.stat: 100+ Grave Goods & Tooth Clues from the Alps
cards.connective: Metal wealth also created powerful Bronze Age leaders and travellers.
cards.html: Rulers wore beaten gold lunulae collars and the gleaming Mold Gold Cape. Near Stonehenge, the Amesbury Archer was buried with five beakers, copper knives, and Alpine tooth clues.
cards.spoken: Metal wealth also created powerful Bronze Age leaders and travellers. <short pause> Rulers wore beaten gold lunulae collars and the gleaming Mold Gold Cape. Near Stonehenge, the Amesbury Archer was buried with five beakers, copper knives, and Alpine tooth clues.

cards.heading: Trade Routes End the Stone Age
cards.stat: Metal Axes, Wider Farmland & European Trade
cards.connective: Shining bronze tools and long trade links reshaped island Britain.
cards.html: Recyclable bronze tools felled thick forests for wider sunny farms across Britain. Guarding copper, tin, and gold routes connected British chieftains to distant European traders.
cards.spoken: Shining bronze tools and long trade links reshaped island Britain. <short pause> Recyclable bronze tools felled thick forests for wider sunny farms across Britain. Guarding copper, tin, and gold routes connected British chieftains to distant European traders .

lesson_4.takeaway: Beaker newcomers introduced metalworking around 2400 BC, and mixing Welsh copper with Cornish tin gave Bronze Age Britain tough cast axes and rich trade links.
vocab: 1. Smelting
Heating crushed metal rock in a hot fire until liquid metal runs out.
2. Bronze
Tough golden metal made by mixing nine parts copper with one part tin.
3. Mould
Hollow two-piece stone shape filled with liquid bronze to cast tools.
lesson_4.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Beaker newcomers introduced metalworking around 2400 BC, and mixing Welsh copper with Cornish tin gave Bronze Age Britain tough cast axes and rich trade links.

lesson_5.title: What Did the Sunken Village at Must Farm Reveal About Bronze Age Homes?
lesson_5.spokenTitle: What did the sunken village at Must Farm reveal about Bronze Age homes?
lesson_5.provenanceNote: British Museum, Royal BC Museum, Historic Environment Scotland & Original Hub Cartography (Zero AI Imagery)

cards.heading: Stilt Homes & Sudden Fire
cards.stat: Airless River Mud Seals 'Britain's Pompeii'
cards.connective: What did the sunken village at Must Farm reveal about Bronze Age homes?
cards.html: Around 900 BC, families built wooden roundhouses on oak stilts above a river at Must Farm. When fire struck, homes dropped into airless waterlogged mud as "Britain's Pompeii".
cards.spoken: What did the sunken village at Must Farm reveal about Bronze Age homes? <short pause> Around 900 BC, families built wooden roundhouses on oak stilts above a river at Must Farm . When fire struck, homes dropped into airless waterlogged mud as "Britain's Pompeii".

cards.heading: Porridge Spoons & Oldest Wheel
cards.stat: 1-Metre Ash Wheel, Cloth & Wicker Eel Traps
cards.connective: Deep wet mud stopped fragile wood, food, and cloth from rotting.
cards.html: Archaeologists uncovered bowls of charred porridge with a wooden spoon, fine woven cloth, and wicker eel traps. Beside marshy Flag Fen lay a one-metre wooden wheel, Britain's oldest!
cards.spoken: Deep wet mud stopped fragile wood, food, and cloth from rotting. <short pause> Archaeologists uncovered bowls of charred porridge with a wooden spoon, fine woven cloth, and wicker eel traps . Beside marshy Flag Fen lay a one-metre wooden wheel , Britain's oldest!

cards.heading: Sacred Waters & Dover Boat
cards.stat: Oak Planks Stitched Together with Yew Twigs
cards.connective: Bronze Age Britons also sailed far beyond their wetland rivers.
cards.html: Mediterranean glass beads reached Must Farm while villagers lowered bronze shields into sacred waters at Flag Fen. Sailors crossed the Channel in the Dover sewn-plank boat stitched with yew.
cards.spoken: Bronze Age Britons also sailed far beyond their wetland rivers. <short pause> Mediterranean glass beads reached Must Farm while villagers lowered bronze shields into sacred waters at Flag Fen . Sailors crossed the Channel in the Dover sewn-plank boat stitched with yew.

cards.heading: A Snapshot of Bronze Age Life
cards.stat: Skilled Carpenters, Weavers & Sea Traders
cards.connective: Must Farm froze one ordinary Bronze Age day in amazing detail.
cards.html: Preserved timbers, wooden wheels, and cosy roundhouse goods proved Bronze Age families were skilled carpenters and weavers. Seagoing oak boats linked British villages straight to Europe.
cards.spoken: Must Farm froze one ordinary Bronze Age day in amazing detail. <short pause> Preserved timbers, wooden wheels , and cosy roundhouse goods proved Bronze Age families were skilled carpenters and weavers . Seagoing oak boats linked British villages straight to Europe.

lesson_5.takeaway: Sealed in wet river mud around 900 BC, Must Farm preserved stilt roundhouses, charred porridge, woven cloth, and Britain's oldest complete wooden wheel.
vocab: 1. Stilts
Sturdy oak posts holding wooden houses safely above river water.
2. Waterlogged
Soaked in airless wet mud that stops wood and cloth from rotting.
3. Sewn-plank boat
Bronze Age oak ship stitched together with twisted yew branches.
lesson_5.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Sealed in wet river mud around 900 BC, Must Farm preserved stilt roundhouses, charred porridge, woven cloth, and Britain's oldest complete wooden wheel.

lesson_6.topicLabel: Enquiry 06: Iron Age Celts & Giant Hillforts
lesson_6.title: How Did Iron Tools and Giant Hillforts Shape Celtic Britain?
lesson_6.spokenTitle: How did iron tools and giant hillforts shape Celtic Britain?
lesson_6.provenanceNote: British Museum, Royal BC Museum, Historic Environment Scotland & Original Hub Cartography (Zero AI Imagery)

cards.heading: Iron Ploughs & Roundhouses
cards.stat: Blacksmith Furnaces, Querns & Thatch Homes
cards.connective: How did iron tools and giant hillforts shape Celtic Britain?
cards.html: From 800 BC, blacksmiths heated local iron ore to hammer tough iron ploughshares that sliced heavy clay soil. Celtic families ground flour on rotary querns inside thatched roundhouses.
cards.spoken: How did iron tools and giant hillforts shape Celtic Britain? <short pause> From 800 BC, blacksmiths heated local iron ore to hammer tough iron ploughshares that sliced heavy clay soil. Celtic families ground flour on rotary querns inside thatched roundhouses.

cards.heading: Celtic Tribes & Maiden Castle
cards.stat: Towering Chalk Ramparts & Slingshot Gates
cards.connective: Bigger harvests grew rival Celtic tribes that needed strong defences.
cards.html: Tribes crowned high ridges with giant hillforts like Maiden Castle in Dorset. Steep earth ramparts, winding gates, and slingshot stones guarded grain pits while chalk hills held the Uffington Horse.
cards.spoken: Bigger harvests grew rival Celtic tribes that needed strong defences. <short pause> Tribes crowned high ridges with giant hillforts like Maiden Castle in Dorset. Steep earth ramparts , winding gates, and slingshot stones guarded grain pits while chalk hills held the Uffington Horse.

cards.heading: Gold Torcs, Coins & AD 43
cards.stat: Snettisham Great Torc & Claudius's Legions
cards.connective: Skilled Celtic smiths and traders soon caught the eye of Rome.
cards.html: Wise Druids memorised laws while smiths twisted gold ropes into the Snettisham Great Torc and minted horse coins. In AD 43, Emperor Claudius invaded with four Roman legions.
cards.spoken: Skilled Celtic smiths and traders soon caught the eye of Rome. <short pause> Wise Druids memorised laws while smiths twisted gold ropes into the Snettisham Great Torc and minted horse coins. In AD 43 , Emperor Claudius invaded with four Roman legions.

cards.heading: Written History Begins in AD 43
cards.stat: 800,000+ Years of British Prehistory Close
cards.connective: Roman soldiers brought Latin writing to a thriving Celtic island.
cards.html: Iron ploughs, towering hillforts, and dazzling gold torcs had built a rich Celtic land. When Roman legions landed in AD 43, British prehistory ended and written history began.
cards.spoken: Roman soldiers brought Latin writing to a thriving Celtic island. <short pause> Iron ploughs, towering hillforts , and dazzling gold torcs had built a rich Celtic land. When Roman legions landed in AD 43, British prehistory ended and written history began.

lesson_6.takeaway: Tough iron ploughs, thatched roundhouses, giant hillforts like Maiden Castle, and gold torcs shaped Celtic Britain until Rome invaded in AD 43.
vocab: 1. Rotary quern
Two heavy round stones spun with a handle to grind grain into flour.
2. Hillfort
Hilltop town ringed by steep earth ramparts, ditches, and gates.
3. Torc
Heavy neck ring twisted from gold or silver worn by Celtic leaders.
lesson_6.spokenTakeaway: Here is the big story in one sentence. <short pause> Tough iron ploughs, thatched roundhouses, giant hillforts like Maiden Castle, and gold torcs shaped Celtic Britain until Rome invaded in AD 43.
